examples.japanese: {早熟|そうじゅく}な{子供|こども}だった。
{早熟|そうじゅく}な{才能|さいのう}を{持|も}つ{音楽家|おんがくか}として{注目|ちゅうもく}された。
examples.english: She attracted attention as a musician with precocious talent.

examples.japanese: {早熟|そうじゅく}な{天才|てんさい}が{大人|おとな}になってからも{活躍|かつやく}するとは{限|かぎ}らない。
examples.english: It is not always the case that a precocious genius remains successful as an adult.

examples.japanese: この{品種|ひんしゅ}は{早熟|そうじゅく}で、{夏|なつ}の{初|はじ}めに{収穫|しゅうかく}できる。
examples.english: This variety ripens early and can be harvested at the beginning of summer.

examples.japanese: {早熟|そうじゅく}{品種|ひんしゅ}は{市場|しじょう}に{早|はや}く{出|だ}せるので{人気|にんき}がある。
examples.english: Early-ripening varieties are popular because they can be brought to market sooner.

examples.japanese: {暖|あたた}かい{気候|きこう}の{地域|ちいき}では{果物|くだもの}が{早熟|そうじゅく}する{傾向|けいこう}がある。
examples.english: In warm climate regions, fruits tend to ripen early.

notes:
Describes development or maturation that occurs earlier than typical. In sense 1, applied to children or young people who show abilities or maturity beyond their age. In sense 2, used in agriculture for crops that ripen ahead of the normal season. Composed of {早|そう} (early) and {熟|じゅく} (mature, ripen).

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {早熟|そうじゅく}な{子|こ}: precocious child
- {早熟|そうじゅく}な{才能|さいのう}: precocious talent
- {早熟|そうじゅく}{品種|ひんしゅ}: early-ripening variety
- {早熟|そうじゅく}{型|がた}: precocious type

SIMILAR WORDS:
- {晩成|ばんせい}: late blooming — the opposite; achieving success later in life
- {大器晩成|たいきばんせい}: great talents mature late — a proverb and idiom
